skill.name: team-dev
skill.description: Organizes independent development tasks into dependency-aware parallel groups and coordinates isolated worktree-based implementation.
skill.summary: Coordinate parallel development agents with task dependencies, isolated worktrees, and staged verification.
skill.author: cubha

security_audit.summary: All 20 external-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown code spans or documentation of optional project verification commands. All four entropy alerts are false positives because the reviewed files are readable Markdown documentation; no encoded payloads, executable code, network access, secret collection, or prompt-injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to run optional project verification commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require agents to show the exact command and request confirmation before running unfamiliar repository scripts, especially verify.sh.

remediation.issue: Parallel agents can make coordinated repository changes.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing file-scope limits and require a final review of each worktree diff before integration.

`run_in_background: true`로 실행했으므로, 각 에이전트 완료 시 자동 알림을 받는다.
| `--auto` | auto 모드 ON — 남은 그룹 전부 자동 진행 |

| `--dry-run` | 의존성 분석 + 그룹 분류만 수행, 실제 구현 안 함 |
| `--tdd` / `--no-tdd` | TDD RED 게이트 발동 / 완전 끔 (Phase 0 참조) |

content.value_statement: Large changes can be slow when independent tasks are completed one at a time. This skill groups dependencies, assigns isolated worktrees, and verifies work before integration.
actual_capabilities: Collects existing tasks or separates a feature request into subtasks.
Classifies subtasks into dependency-aware parallel execution groups.
Uses isolated Git worktrees for parallel implementation agents.
Supports interactive approval, automatic group progression, and dry-run planning.
Applies a test-first RED gate to eligible logic tasks when TDD is enabled.
Coordinates per-task and integrated project verification when scripts are available.
limitations: Requires a Git repository because it uses worktree isolation.
Works best when tasks modify independent files or modules.
Does not guarantee that repository verification scripts are safe or complete.
Limits parallel implementation to five agents and requires human judgment for uncertain merge conflicts.

use_cases.title: Plan a feature split
use_cases.description: Break a multi-module feature into ordered groups before any implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Implement independent components
use_cases.description: Assign separate UI, API, and utility tasks to isolated agents when their files do not overlap.

use_cases.title: Review parallel delivery
use_cases.description: Use staged verification and integration reports to review a team of coding agents.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a task plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /team-dev --dry-run to split this feature into dependency groups: add profile editing, avatar upload, and account validation.

prompt_templates.title: Run an approved feature plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /team-dev to implement these independent tasks: add a settings API, create its tests, and add a settings navigation link. Ask for approval before dispatch.

prompt_templates.title: Use selective TDD
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /team-dev --tdd for these tasks: add validation rules, add validation unit tests, and update the account settings form. Keep UI tasks test-after.

prompt_templates.title: Automate independent groups
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /team-dev --auto --tdd to implement the approved independent tasks. Stop and report if integrated verification fails.

output_examples.input: Split a user-settings feature into parallel work.
output: Group 1: validation rules and navigation updates run in parallel.
Group 2: settings form waits for validation rules.
Each completed task reports changed files and verification status.

output_examples.input: Run a dry-run for three dependent API tasks.
output: Dependency plan identifies the shared type as the first task.
Endpoint and client tasks are scheduled after the shared type.
No agents are dispatched and no files are changed.

best_practices: Use --dry-run to review dependencies before implementation.
Keep each subtask limited to clearly owned files.
Review worktree diffs and verification results before integration.
anti_patterns: Do not use parallel groups for tasks that modify the same file.
Do not enable automatic progression for an unreviewed task plan.
Do not treat a passing project script as a complete security review.

faq.question: Does this skill require Git?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Git worktrees to isolate concurrent implementation work.

faq.question: What does --dry-run do?
faq.answer: It analyzes dependencies and prints execution groups without dispatching implementation agents.

faq.question: When should I use --auto?
faq.answer: Use it only after reviewing the task plan. It continues through remaining groups until verification fails.

faq.question: How does TDD work?
faq.answer: Eligible logic tasks can write and confirm a failing test before implementation when TDD is enabled.

faq.question: Can tasks edit the same file?
faq.answer: No. Shared-file changes should be placed in separate sequential groups to reduce merge conflicts.

faq.question: Does the skill resolve every merge conflict?
faq.answer: No. It requires user confirmation when an automatic conflict resolution is uncertain.
